residency_mobility: Residency can be possible but not “easy”

residency_mobility: Immigration/residency pathways are limited vs. U.S. mainland
notes: Tax baseline: IRS treats virtual currency/digital assets as property; territory residency rules differ (IRC §937 + American Samoa system). (IRS)

name: Andorra
legal_clarity: Dedicated digital assets / DLT legal framework (Law 24/2022)
tax_treatment: Generally low-tax jurisdiction; crypto treatment depends on classification but operates under a modernized framework
banking_fiat_rails: Banking is sophisticated but onboarding can be strict
residency_mobility: Passive residency commonly requires significant investment thresholds (not “easy,” but possible)
notes: Andorra has Law 24/2022 addressing digital representation of assets via cryptography/DLT/blockchain. (CASES & LACAMBRA) Residency: passive residency guides commonly cite large investment/deposit requirements (verify with official counsel for current thresholds). (Immigrant Invest)

name: Angola
legal_clarity: Mining crackdown + limited broader framework
tax_treatment: Unclear/limited published crypto tax guidance
banking_fiat_rails: Rails constrained; compliance risk elevated
residency_mobility: Residency typically difficult unless work/investment
notes: Parliament approved a crypto mining ban with criminal penalties (effective 2024 per reporting). (Bloomberg Law) Broader crypto regulation remains limited/unclear in many summaries.

name: Anguilla
legal_clarity: Digital Assets Business Act (licensing regime)
tax_treatment: Typically tax-neutral reputation, but crypto-specific tax treatment should be confirmed for your structure
banking_fiat_rails: Offshore rails exist; de-risking/compliance can be a factor
residency_mobility: Residency is not “easy” for most without ties/investment
notes: Anguilla has a Digital Assets Business Act establishing licensing/supervision for digital asset business. (fsc.org.ai)

name: Antarctica
legal_clarity: No sovereign legal/tax regime
tax_treatment: N/A
banking_fiat_rails: No retail banking system
residency_mobility: No residency (research stations only)
notes: Antarctica has no permanent cities/population and no normal immigration/residency regime; activity is governed by national programs + the Antarctic Treaty system. (Wikipedia)

name: Antigua and Barbuda
legal_clarity: Digital Assets Business Act (licensing regime)
tax_treatment: Often cited as capital-gains-tax-free; confirm personal/corporate specifics for your profile
banking_fiat_rails: Functional rails but can be correspondent-bank sensitive
residency_mobility: Strong mobility via Citizenship by Investment pathways
notes: Antigua’s Digital Assets Business Act provides a licensing framework. (Antigua and Barbuda Laws) Official CBI authority: CIU. (Citizenship by Investment Programme)

name: Argentina
legal_clarity: Regulated VASP perimeter developing
tax_treatment: Tax applies; inflation/FX controls complicate real outcomes
banking_fiat_rails: On/off-ramps exist but FX controls + bank restrictions can be meaningful
residency_mobility: Residency often attainable via income-based routes
notes: Argentina introduced/expanded VASP registration requirements under CNV regulation (2025 summaries). (Dentons)

name: Armenia
legal_clarity: New crypto-asset legal framework (effective 2025)
tax_treatment: Tax treatment typically under general income rules unless specific regime applies
banking_fiat_rails: Rails generally workable; compliance evolving
residency_mobility: Temporary residence pathways exist (work/study/family)
notes: Armenia’s crypto-asset law changes took effect in 2025 (professional summaries). (CIA) Residency eligibility for temporary resident card (official MFA page). (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Armenia)

name: Aruba
legal_clarity: AML/CTF + supervision approach for VASPs
tax_treatment: Tax depends on residency/status; crypto-specific guidance limited publicly
banking_fiat_rails: Rails available but cautious
residency_mobility: Residency possible; not “instant,” varies by basis
notes: Aruba’s central bank placed VASPs under supervision effective Sept 8, 2021. (cbaruba.org)

name: Australia
legal_clarity: Very clear, but aggressively enforced; crypto fully embedded in surveillance & AML regime
tax_treatment: Crypto treated as property; CGT applies to almost all disposals; no de minimis; staking, airdrops, forks taxed as income; extensive record-keeping obligations
banking_fiat_rails: Technically strong, practically hostile: widespread de-banking, transfer blocks to exchanges, enhanced SoF scrutiny; retail users frequently locked out
residency_mobility: One of the hardest OECD countries to immigrate to; points-based, slow, expensive; no crypto-friendly residency path
notes: Australia offers clarity without freedom. While crypto is legal and guidance is extensive, the regime is tax-punitive, surveillance-heavy, and hostile at the banking layer. Everyday BTC users face CGT on trivial transactions, aggressive ATO data matching, and frequent bank transfer blocks to exchanges. There is no meaningful privacy, no tax advantage, and no easy residency pathway. Australia works only for fully compliant, high-friction users who accept constant reporting and limited banking tolerance.

name: Austria
legal_clarity: High clarity (EU context + national guidance)
tax_treatment: Austria provides detailed official guidance on taxation of cryptocurrencies (incl. reporting/withholding mechanics)
banking_fiat_rails: Strong SEPA/Euro rails
residency_mobility: Residency moderate-to-hard (EU/third-country differences)
notes: Austrian Finance Ministry (BMF) publishes crypto tax guidance (official). (bmf.gv.at)

name: Azerbaijan
legal_clarity: Developing / partial (sandbox activity; not legal tender)
tax_treatment: Limited clear public crypto tax guidance
banking_fiat_rails: Rails likely limited; compliance risk
residency_mobility: Short visits easy; residency moderate

name: Bahamas
legal_clarity: Clear digital-asset framework (DARE Act + licensing regime); crypto legal to hold/use via regulated providers.
tax_treatment: 0% personal income tax / 0% capital gains tax (no income/CGT system).
banking_fiat_rails: Decent rails for residents; international wires/PSPs exist but compliance can be strict; some de-risking for crypto-linked flows.
residency_mobility: Residency via investment/permanent residency possible but paperwork-heavy; not “easy” vs. true nomad hubs.
notes: DARE Act is a real plus; “tax heaven” is real, but bank compliance is the bottleneck (expect KYC/SoF scrutiny).

name: Bahrain
legal_clarity: Very clear CBB rules for crypto-asset services (regulated module + licensing). (cbben.thomsonreuters.com)
tax_treatment: 0% personal income tax; no CGT regime for individuals (VAT exists but not a “gains tax”).
banking_fiat_rails: Strong regional banking/fintech hub; regulated rails generally workable for compliant users/businesses.
residency_mobility: “Golden Residency” style programs exist, but most expats still rely on sponsorship/employment; not plug-and-play.
notes: One of the clearest Middle East regulators for crypto rails; good for compliant operators.

name: Bangladesh
legal_clarity: Bangladesh Bank has treated crypto as illegal/unauthorized; high enforcement risk. (ResearchGate)
tax_treatment: Not meaningfully applicable for legal planning (activity may be illegal).
banking_fiat_rails: Fiat rails effectively blocked for crypto; high account-risk.
residency_mobility: Residency not designed for “move-for-freedom”; difficult for most foreigners.
notes: Not a viable “bitcoin-friendly” jurisdiction today due to illegality and rail risk.

name: Barbados
legal_clarity: Generally permissive stance; has been positioning for fintech/virtual-asset business frameworks (varies by activity).
tax_treatment: 0% capital gains tax (Barbados generally has no CGT); income tax can apply if treated as business income.
banking_fiat_rails: Rails exist but can be conservative with crypto-linked flows; expect compliance friction.
residency_mobility: Welcome Stamp (remote work) exists; residency is relatively approachable for long-stays vs many countries.
notes: Attractive lifestyle + no CGT; still, banking can be the limiting factor (documentation matters).

name: Belarus

residency_mobility: Residency possible but geopolitical risk is the real blocker.

residency_mobility: EU residency routes exist but not “easy”; bureaucracy high, taxes/social contributions heavy.
notes: Very strong rails + rule of law, but not “freedom-focused” and taxes are no longer favorable for crypto.

name: Belize
legal_clarity: No single marquee crypto statute; generally permissive but not a top-tier regulated hub.
tax_treatment: Territorial-style outcomes often marketed; no capital gains tax is a practical advantage, but treatment depends on residency/source and structuring. (belizefsc.org.bz)
banking_fiat_rails: Banking can be difficult (de-risking); expect slower onboarding and higher documentation burden.
residency_mobility: Residency options exist (including retirement programs); moderate ease vs developed countries.
notes: Good “paper” tax story; real-world constraint is bank access and compliance.

name: Benin

residency_mobility: Residency not designed as a global nomad hub; practical ease is limited.

name: Bermuda

residency_mobility: Residency is hard/expensive; not an “easy move” jurisdiction.

residency_mobility: Residency is difficult; tourism-oriented, not an easy long-term move.

banking_fiat_rails: Crypto-friendly banking incl. Towerbank; government acceptance for public payments
residency_mobility: Friendly Nations / investment residency comparatively easy
notes:
Panama is one of the few countries where Bitcoin actually works end-to-end in practice. It uses a territorial tax system, meaning foreign-sourced income is not taxed, so for most residents Bitcoin gains are effectively taxed at 0%. This isn’t a loophole or temporary incentive — it’s core tax law.
Unlike many “crypto-friendly” jurisdictions, Panama has real banking support. Local banks such as Towerbank openly service crypto users and businesses, making fiat on- and off-ramps usable without elaborate offshore structures. That alone puts Panama in a very small global club.
The government has also shown real acceptance. Public services and municipal payments can be made in Bitcoin through approved channels, which significantly lowers political and regulatory risk. Countries that integrate Bitcoin into public payments are far less likely to reverse course.
Residency is realistically attainable. Programs like Friendly Nations and investment pathways allow people to become residents without extreme capital requirements, while avoiding aggressive global income reporting or lifestyle surveillance.
Finally, Panama is boring in the best possible way. It runs on USD, has a stable banking system, is politically neutral, and functions as a global hub between North and South America. For Bitcoin users, that combination of low tax, usable banks, and low hostility makes Panama one of the strongest practical jurisdictions in the world.

tax_treatment: No administrable tax regime
banking_fiat_rails: No reliable rails
residency_mobility: Residency not practical
notes: State capacity dominates; crypto legality irrelevant

name: South Africa
legal_clarity: Clear, regulated: FSCA licenses Crypto Asset Service Providers (CASPs) under FAIS/CASP regime. (DLA Piper)
tax_treatment: SARS: crypto taxed under normal income tax rules; CGT effective up to ~18% (40% inclusion × 45% top marginal), or income up to 45% if trading. (South African Revenue Service)
banking_fiat_rails: Rails solid regionally; compliant exchanges exist, but banks are AML/SoF strict.
residency_mobility: Residency moderate (work/business/investment); not “easy residency” vs hubs.
notes: Strong “rule-of-law + rails”; not tax-light, but actually operable (licensed providers).

name: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
legal_clarity: Not a practical jurisdiction (UK overseas territory; no normal resident economy).
tax_treatment: N/A
banking_fiat_rails: No meaningful rails for civilians.
residency_mobility: No residency pathway.
notes: Treat as non-jurisdiction for BTC friendliness.

name: South Sudan
legal_clarity: No meaningful crypto framework; severe instability dominates.
tax_treatment: No reliable crypto tax regime.
banking_fiat_rails: Rails extremely weak.
residency_mobility: Residency not practical.
notes: Not viable for BTC ops/residency due to state capacity constraints.

name: Spain
legal_clarity: Clear EU legality; high compliance/reporting expectations.
tax_treatment: Crypto gains taxed as savings income: 19% / 21% / 23% / 27% / 30% (≥€300k at 30% from 2025). (PwC Tax Summaries)
banking_fiat_rails: Strong SEPA rails; banks AML-sensitive but functional.
residency_mobility: Residency moderate-to-hard (EU processes; bureaucracy).
notes: Strong rails but not “freedom focused.” Also watch reporting obligations (e.g., foreign holdings reporting regimes).

name: Sri Lanka
legal_clarity: Crypto legality/regulation uncertain and conservative; usage exists but policy risk is meaningful.
tax_treatment: No stable, widely relied crypto tax guidance; assume general income rules (uncertain).
banking_fiat_rails: Rails constrained; bank tolerance limited.
residency_mobility: Residency not a mobility hub.
notes: Not a friendly rails jurisdiction; treat as medium policy risk.

name: Sudan
legal_clarity: No practical supportive framework; sanctions/conflict and weak institutions dominate.
tax_treatment: No reliable crypto tax regime.
banking_fiat_rails: Rails weak; high friction.
residency_mobility: Residency not practical for mobility.
notes: Not viable as a BTC base in practice.

name: Suriname
legal_clarity: No mature crypto framework; generally unregulated/unclear.
tax_treatment: No clear crypto tax guidance; likely general income rules (uncertain).
banking_fiat_rails: Rails modest; compliance friction.
residency_mobility: Residency moderate (work/invest).
notes: Not hostile, but not a crypto hub; banking depth is limited.

name: Svalbard and Jan Mayen
legal_clarity: Norwegian territory; Svalbard has special treaty status but not a normal “tax/crypto jurisdiction” play.
tax_treatment: Norway tax rules generally apply in practice; crypto gains taxed 22% (capital income), plus reporting.
banking_fiat_rails: Rails limited locally; relies on Norway.
residency_mobility: Residency is highly restricted (Svalbard residency is unusual but not a mainstream mobility route).
notes: Not practical as a BTC base despite interesting legal status.

name: Sweden
legal_clarity: Clear legality; strong reporting culture.
tax_treatment: Crypto capital gains taxed 30%; only 70% of losses deductible commonly cited. (Koinly)
banking_fiat_rails: Excellent rails; very AML strict.
residency_mobility: Residency hard (Nordic, costly).
notes: Predictable but not bitcoin-tax-friendly.

name: Switzerland
legal_clarity: Very clear + crypto-mature; canton-driven practice; strong legal environment. (GLI)
tax_treatment: 0% income tax on private capital gains (if classified as private investor); wealth tax applies; staking/interest-like income can be taxable. (RSM Global)
banking_fiat_rails: World-class rails; banks are selective but crypto-capable (high compliance).
residency_mobility: Residency is hard/expensive; permits controlled.
notes: One of the top “serious” BTC jurisdictions for compliant holders/companies; not anonymity-oriented. Lugano (“Plan ₿”) is the standout: the city treats Bitcoin and USDT as usable payment methods for municipal services (including taxes/fees) via a managed payments flow (instant conversion to CHF).

name: Syrian Arab Republic
legal_clarity: Not viable: sanctions, conflict, and state capacity constraints dominate.
tax_treatment: No reliable crypto tax regime.
banking_fiat_rails: Rails non-functional for compliant international use.
residency_mobility: Residency not practical.
notes: Not a practical jurisdiction regardless of informal crypto usage.

name: Taiwan, Province of China
legal_clarity: Crypto legal; regulated under AML/financial supervision; decent clarity for compliant activity.
tax_treatment: Taxed under general income/capital rules (classification-dependent); no single simple headline rate.
banking_fiat_rails: Strong rails; compliance-heavy.
residency_mobility: Residency moderate-to-hard (work/investment routes).
notes: Operationally strong if compliant; not “low tax” and not privacy-maximal.

name: Tajikistan
legal_clarity: No mature crypto framework; uncertain policy environment.
tax_treatment: No clear crypto tax guidance (uncertain).
banking_fiat_rails: Rails limited; higher friction.
residency_mobility: Residency not easy; not a mobility hub.
notes: Not friendly in practice due to weak rails and uncertainty.

name: Tanzania, United Republic of
legal_clarity: No comprehensive crypto regime; tends to be cautious; practical clarity limited.
tax_treatment: No clear crypto tax guidance broadly relied upon; uncertainty.
banking_fiat_rails: Rails exist but conservative; crypto-linked banking can be difficult.
residency_mobility: Residency moderate (work/invest).
notes: Not hostile, but not a “bitcoin rails” jurisdiction.

name: Thailand
legal_clarity: Clearer: regulated digital-asset operators; policy actively supportive for licensed routes.
tax_treatment: PIT exemption on capital gains from digital assets via licensed operators (Jan 1, 2025–Dec 31, 2029). (Forvis Mazars)
banking_fiat_rails: Rails workable; strongest if using licensed Thai operators; AML still real.
residency_mobility: Residency moderate (Elite visa and other routes exist but paid/structured).
notes: Big upgrade vs “high-tax Asia” because the exemption is real (but conditions matter: licensed operators). (Forvis Mazars)

name: Timor-Leste

tax_treatment: No clear crypto tax guidance.
banking_fiat_rails: Weak rails; high friction.
residency_mobility: Residency not a mobility hub.
notes: Not hostile, but impractical for BTC ops.

name: Togo
legal_clarity: No dedicated crypto framework; largely unregulated/unclear.
tax_treatment: No clear crypto tax guidance.
banking_fiat_rails: WAEMU rails; banks conservative; P2P likely dominant.
residency_mobility: Residency moderate (work/invest).
notes: Neutral but underdeveloped for rails and regulation.

name: Trinidad and Tobago

tax_treatment: No clear crypto tax headline; likely ordinary income rules if enforced (uncertain).

residency_mobility: Residency moderate.

name: Tunisia
legal_clarity: Legal/unclear
tax_treatment: Mixed/unknown
banking_fiat_rails: Mixed/unknown
residency_mobility: Unknown

name: Turkey
legal_clarity: Crypto holding/trading legal; crypto payments banned since April 2021 (CBRT regulation) (Global Practice Guides)
tax_treatment: Tax treatment exists under general rules; not “tax-light” and reporting/compliance is increasing (rates depend on classification) (Trade.gov)
banking_fiat_rails: Rails workable via major exchanges, but banking can be compliance-friction; payments ban reduces merchant utility (Global Practice Guides)
residency_mobility: Residency: moderate (property/work routes; not “easy” like top residency hubs)
notes: Big market + liquidity, but not freedom-maximal (payments prohibited; strong compliance posture). (Global Practice Guides)

name: Turkmenistan
legal_clarity: New law regulates mining and exchanges effective Jan 1, 2026; crypto not legal tender (Reuters)
tax_treatment: Tax specifics not yet widely operationalized; treat as uncertain while the new regime beds in (Reuters)
banking_fiat_rails: Rails likely limited and heavily controlled despite legalization; high censorship/controls remain (AP News)
residency_mobility: Residency extremely restrictive historically; modest e-visa steps don’t equal easy residency (AP News)
notes: Major “headline legalization” but real usability is likely low (controls + banking depth). (AP News)

name: Turks and Caicos Islands
legal_clarity: No bespoke crypto regime; generally permissive; small market (Freeman Law)
tax_treatment: 0% income / 0% CGT (tax-neutral jurisdiction) (Legal 500)
banking_fiat_rails: Rails limited (small territory); banking is relationship-driven and conservative
residency_mobility: Residency: moderate (not a mass-residency hub; high cost; pathways exist)
notes: Excellent tax profile; weakest link is banking depth/coverage. (Legal 500)

name: Tuvalu
legal_clarity: No crypto framework; tiny market
tax_treatment: No clear crypto tax guidance
banking_fiat_rails: Very limited rails
residency_mobility: Residency not mobility-focused
notes: Not practical for BTC operations.

name: Uganda
legal_clarity: Crypto not legal tender; regulator has warned; banks/fintechs told not to facilitate crypto trade (historically) (TechCrunch)
tax_treatment: No clear crypto tax regime that’s reliably applied; uncertainty
banking_fiat_rails: Rails constrained by supervisory posture; P2P dominates (TechCrunch)
residency_mobility: Residency moderate (work/invest), not a “mobility hub”
notes: Usage exists, but formal rails are the limiter. (TechCrunch)

name: Ukraine
legal_clarity: Virtual assets not prohibited, but full VA regime not yet in force; payment use restricted (GLI)
tax_treatment: Tax framework still evolving; draft efforts ongoing (EY)
banking_fiat_rails: Rails materially impacted by war risk; compliance/on-ramps uneven
residency_mobility: Residency not a typical mobility play (and current risk is high)
notes: Large crypto community, but regime incomplete + war risk dominates. (GLI)

name: United Arab Emirates
legal_clarity: Very clear in practice (VARA/ADGM/DIFC ecosystems); crypto activity widely supported via licensed routes (Ape Law)
tax_treatment: 0% personal income tax / 0% capital gains tax for individuals (Ape Law)
banking_fiat_rails: Top-tier rails; banks still strict on source-of-funds, but crypto-capable ecosystem is deep (Ape Law)
residency_mobility: Residency: comparatively accessible via work/invest/business setup (but not “instant”)
notes: Elite “BTC-friendly” for compliant operators; not privacy/anonymity-oriented. (Ape Law)

name: United Kingdom
legal_clarity: Legal; FCA-led regulatory perimeter expanding; new comprehensive regime scheduled to come into force Oct 25, 2027 (FCA)
tax_treatment: Taxed under CGT/income tax rules; reporting tightening (CARF-related enforcement focus) (Financial Times)
banking_fiat_rails: Excellent rails; very compliance-heavy; exchange access is mature
residency_mobility: Residency: hard (work/family routes; high cost)
notes: Strong rails + rule-of-law, but not low-tax and increasingly surveilled/reporting-driven. (Financial Times)

name: United States
legal_clarity: Crypto legal; IRS treats digital assets as property (IRS)
tax_treatment: Federal: long-term CG 0/15/20%; short-term at ordinary rates; NIIT can apply (Kiplinger)
banking_fiat_rails: Best-in-class rails, but very strict compliance (KYC, reporting)
residency_mobility: Residency hard (immigration-based)
notes: Amazing rails + liquidity, but high tax/reporting burden; not “freedom-maximal.” (IRS)

name: United States Minor Outlying Islands
legal_clarity: Mostly uninhabited U.S. territories; not a practical jurisdiction
tax_treatment: N/A
banking_fiat_rails: No meaningful rails
residency_mobility: No residency pathway
notes: Treat as non-jurisdiction for your index.

name: Uruguay
legal_clarity: Crypto generally permitted; no special crypto regime driving clarity
tax_treatment: No individual capital gains tax (Uruguay generally does not tax individual CG in the same way); territorial-style outcomes can be favorable (PwC Tax Summaries)
banking_fiat_rails: Rails decent for LATAM; banking can be conservative for crypto-source funds
residency_mobility: Residency: moderate and often attractive for relocation in the region; tax-holiday proposals exist for new residents (policy can change) (tagalliances.com)
notes: Good “lifestyle + potential tax advantages” jurisdiction; still not a top crypto-banking hub. (tagalliances.com)

name: Uzbekistan
legal_clarity: Clear rule: crypto activity allowed through licensed providers; regulated lists exist (napp.uz)
tax_treatment: Special tax regime exists for foreign citizens via authorized exchanges; “crypto income not taxed” is asserted by some summaries but treat as scoped/specific (napp.uz)
banking_fiat_rails: Rails are restrictive (must route via domestic licensed VASPs); practical flexibility limited (Asterium)
residency_mobility: Residency: moderate; not a prime mobility hub
notes: Strong formal control model: compliant paths exist, but it’s not “free.” (Asterium)

name: Vanuatu
legal_clarity: VASP licensing framework: VASPs must be licensed by VFSC (vfsc.vu)
tax_treatment: Often marketed as tax-light; crypto-specific tax headline not definitive—treat as generally favorable but verify for your case
banking_fiat_rails: Rails limited; reputation/derisking can be an issue despite licensing
residency_mobility: Residency: moderate (investment pathways exist; not “instant”)
notes: Good for offshore structures if compliant, but rails and counterparties can be limiting. (vfsc.vu)

name: Venezuela, Bolivarian Republic of
legal_clarity: Legal status complicated: crypto widely used, but regulator dysfunction and enforcement swings are real; SUNACRIP operations disrupted since 2023 (Lightspark)
tax_treatment: Tax not reliably “plan-able”; enforcement/institutional capacity issues dominate
banking_fiat_rails: Rails highly constrained; sanctions/compliance risk high; many rely on informal stablecoin rails (El País)
residency_mobility: Residency not a mobility play; high risk
notes: High adoption ≠ friendly jurisdiction: sanctions + regulator instability are the core risk. (Proelium Law LLP)

name: Viet Nam
legal_clarity: Crypto not legal tender / not a lawful means of payment; moving toward a licensed exchange pilot framework (vietnamnews.vn)
tax_treatment: Tax treatment not a clean headline; expect general income rules + evolving compliance as the framework matures
banking_fiat_rails: Rails improving mainly through licensed channels; still compliance-heavy and historically restrictive on payment use (vietnamnews.vn)
residency_mobility: Residency moderate (work/investment); not a residency hub
notes: Direction is improving (licensing regime), but payment illegality keeps it from top-tier friendliness. (vietnamnews.vn)

name: Virgin Islands, British
legal_clarity: Clear and widely used offshore framework; tax-neutral; VASP obligations exist
tax_treatment: 0% income tax / no CGT; crypto tax guidance not formalized but neutrality dominates (GLI)
banking_fiat_rails: Rails are offshore-oriented; banking is selective and documentation-heavy
residency_mobility: Residency limited (not a common relocation base)
notes: Excellent for compliant structures; not a “live-and-bank-easily” jurisdiction for most individuals. (GLI)

name: Virgin Islands, U.S.
legal_clarity: U.S. principles apply (crypto as property); local incentive programs can benefit businesses (EDC/RTPark) (armenian-lawyer.com)
tax_treatment: Generally U.S.-style taxation for individuals; business incentives can reduce effective rates for qualifying structures (Global Practice Guides)
banking_fiat_rails: U.S.-linked rails; compliance-heavy
residency_mobility: Residency: mainly for those who can legitimately relocate under U.S. rules; not a visa solution for non-U.S. persons
notes: More “U.S. with local business incentives” than a pure BTC tax haven. (Global Practice Guides)

name: Wallis and Futuna
legal_clarity: French overseas collectivity (France/EU rules apply; tiny market)
tax_treatment: France PFU 30% for typical private-investor crypto gains
banking_fiat_rails: Very limited rails due to remoteness/scale
residency_mobility: Residency effectively French-administered; not easy
notes: Essentially “France, but impractical.”

tax_treatment: Not reliably plan-able
banking_fiat_rails: Rails weak/uncertain
residency_mobility: Residency not practical
notes: Treat as out-of-scope for serious jurisdiction selection.

residency_mobility: Residency not practical

notes: Not hostile in a single “ban” sense, but practical usability is limited by rails/policy risk.
